questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: What is the single most effective thing you can do to survive an accident?

options.text: Ask others about how to ride more safely.

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: Which item does NOT need to be checked regularly?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous in traffic.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are slippery surfaces. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic there.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because they have the most conflict between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on a slippery surface. Sudden moves on slippery surfaces can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid a slippery road.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This takes just a few minutes and helps prevent dangerous problems before you enter traffic.

questions.question: What must you have when carrying a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: A seat large enough for two riders.
Don't ask the passenger to wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat for two riders. Your motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you do.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed, which increases danger.

questions.question: What happens when you combine alcohol and over-the-counter drugs?

options.text: The side effects of both cancel each other out.
It will not affect your riding abilities.

questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can impair your riding ability. Some medicines become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: At all times, no matter the weather.
Only on rides longer than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, no matter the weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding. It protects you even in warm weather. A jacket helps protect you from the sun and prevents dehydration.

questions.question: A motorcycle has the best traction on which surface?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates all reduce traction and are hazardous for motorcycles.

questions.question: A rectangular sign can be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These signs show traffic rules. You must follow all rules on these signs.

questions.question: When you drink alcohol quickly:

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body removes the alcohol faster.
The effects of alcohol are reduced.
You are less likely to be stopped by police.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol quickly causes more alcohol to build up in your body. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: If you drink just one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on your body.
Drinking coffee will remove the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your judgment and riding ability. Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. Coffee does not help.

questions.question: The body removes about one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.
